# Atrium Nutrislice source evidence

Observed September 10, 2026 New York (September 11 around 01:14 UTC). Discover from [Rutgers' school index](https://rutgers.api.nutrislice.com/menu/api/schools/), not a guessed identifier: **71385, The Atrium, `the-atrium`, 126 College Avenue, America/New_York**. The index advertises Breakfast 32934, Lunch 33316, Dinner 33318 and Late Knight 33385. KnightBite keeps its existing three-meal interface; the separately published 18-item Late Knight menu is not imported or relabeled Dinner.

Real weekly responses cover September 6–12. September 10 contains 42 Breakfast, 167 Lunch and 167 Dinner foods, with 7/26/26 station headers. Lunch and Dinner are separate requested menu types but contain identical food lists that day. Tests must not manufacture a distinction in captured source data. A separate synthetic Livingston fixture still proves three distinct meal contents.

For KnightBite's six nutrients, 39/42 Breakfast and 161/167 Lunch and Dinner foods contain all six fields. Partial foods remain partial; quantities supplied as zero remain zero. These coverage counts describe top-level metadata before portion selection. Atrium follows `serving_size_info` / an entry override into the unique matching `food_sizes` nutrition when size records are supplied, like the published UI; otherwise it uses `rounded_nutrition_info`. Both go through the unchanged shared normalizer. After conservative portion matching, 35/42 Breakfast and 155/167 Lunch/Dinner records have all six tracked nutrients; every food remains accessible. In a supplied size table, missing/ambiguous matches or missing fields stay unknown; absence of a size table uses the inline aggregate with the existing null handling. Other micronutrients, an alternate-size chooser, and Nutrislice's separate Late Knight menu are not implemented. Some foods offer additional `food_sizes` in the published interface; the alternate-size chooser is not imported. The default 6 oz OATMEAL dialog reports 80 kcal, 3g protein and 0g sugar; its conflicting top-level metadata reports 4g protein/1g sugar. A focused regression verifies the published matching-size values and rejects ambiguity instead of filling from top-level metadata. Default returned food records and any distinct entry-level portion variants are preserved, with existing collision-safe identities.

Published-interface comparison was performed by selecting Atrium from Rutgers' location list, then the September 10 Breakfast, Lunch and Dinner links. HOT CEREAL's COUNTRY STYLE GRITS shows **6 oz, 140 kcal, 2g protein, 15g carbs, 0.2g fat, 207mg sodium, 0g sugar**. Lunch's CHICKEN NOODLE SOUP shows **6 ozl, 85 kcal, 7g protein, 9g carbs, 2.5g fat, 391mg sodium, 2g sugar**; Dinner also lists this soup at 85 kcal. These match their API default records. The published section names match the captures. This is representative comparison, not independent nutritional/allergen validation.

- `school.json`: public identity, address, timezone and advertised menu metadata. No authentication headers/cookies or account data.
- `breakfast.json`, `lunch.json`, `dinner.json`: compact September 10 fixtures retaining **every** header/food and all normalization fields. Asset URLs and unrelated metadata omitted. Browser harness deliberately rewrites the date to its controlled requested date; these are offline fixtures, never production fallback.
- `*-week-2026-09-06.json.gz`: full response structure with public asset URL values replaced by equal-length `x` strings. Public food, serving, nutrition and structural metadata retained. Compressed for repository size; tests decompress before the unchanged 8 MiB/500,000-node budget and daily conservation assertions. No day/items are removed. Fixture serialization differs from raw HTTP bytes; [source-api.json](../../../../docs/audits/production-readiness-2026-09-10/atrium-nutrislice-evidence/source-api.json) records both sizes, original hashes, URLs, coverage and counts.

Raw response bytes: Breakfast 1,581,397; Lunch 6,203,507; Dinner 6,203,507. All three full sanitized weeks fit unchanged bounds and preserve every accepted daily food. This adds one representative week, not peak-season coverage or continuing availability. No FoodProNet enrichment, mock substitute, alternate hall/date or nutrition inference is permitted. Unmapped sections remain accessible in More stations, search and List view.
